_comment: Which jurisdictions this build can read, and how. Every service URL here was queried live on 2026-09-07; do not add an entry that has not been. This catalog can name, order, configure and disable sources — it cannot define one, so adding a state on either generic adapter needs no app release, while a county needing Maricopa-depth judgement does.

04._comment: The bespoke ADOT sources run FIRST (compiledFirst) because they encode judgement the HPMS tables cannot: selecting between two coincident route namespaces 2 m apart, excluding the 'L - Local (Non-ADOT)' route type, gating ownership on Owner == DOT, and recovering a TRACS number from free text. HPMS then answers everywhere they do not, which is most of the state: the route layer is 132581 features and 126320 of them are 'Non-ADOT Rte'. Ownership_Value is the find - 218 values shaped 'PHX-Phoenix (4)' giving both the body and its HPMS code, so Tucson, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Scottsdale and Peoria are all named without a single city-level profile, along with 21600 private and 10213 gated-association segments. YearLastConstruction is only 7264 events and is essentially the state system, the same ground ATIS already covers more richly.
04.dateCaveat: ADOT records a construction year for about 7,000 stretches, nearly all of them state routes; elsewhere in Arizona it names the owner but publishes no date.

48.dateCaveat: On the state system TxDOT publishes its construction register back to 1970. Off it there is no statewide record at all, and what a city street shows depends entirely on whether that city publishes one.
48._comment: The inventory is one layer of 133 fields over 1027891 statewide segments and not one field is a street name, so the names are joined from TxDOT_Roadways on GID, which is 1:1 and coerces from the integer to a quoted where clause. ADMIN is the ownership field and is NOT HPMS: it runs 1-16 where HPMS defines nothing at 5-10 or 13-16. See CodeTables.txdotAdmin for the HSYS cross-tab it was derived from. MAP_LBL is a map *shield* label, not a name: on-system rows carry '35', '175', '10C' and toll rows carry '_', so the join is filtered to SYSTEM='Off' and '_' is a null string. Interstates and state highways are therefore named by TIGER, which spells them out. SURF_TREAT_YEAR is populated on only 109233 of 1027891 rows and is a last-surface-treatment date rather than a construction year, so it is deliberately not mapped to yearBuilt; values run back to 1918.

42.dateCaveat: PennDOT publishes a construction year only for roads it maintains itself.
42._comment: JURIS is the ownership field: 1 PennDOT (101354), 2 Turnpike Commission (685), 5 local (11737), 6 interstate bridge commission (51). MAINT_RESPON_IND looks like HPMS-times-ten and is not — every downtown Philadelphia segment reads 40, including I-676 at 64768 AADT, and it is populated only on JURIS=1 rows. YR_BUILT is 0 on every JURIS=5 segment, hence nullNumbers.

22.dateCaveat: Louisiana publishes a construction year for its own control sections, not for local streets.
22._comment: Layer 49 'Louisiana Roadways' is 576063 features statewide and does include residential streets, so name and owner reach local roads here. Layer 91 is listed before layer 49's own Ownership copy on purpose: the two disagree — Balis Dr reads Ownership 2 on 49 and 4 on 91 — and 91 is the dedicated HPMS event table with measures. Layer 3 'Local Road Names' is empty; do not wire it. RouteID runs two namespaces in one service: '013-04-1-010' for control sections and '033900412201591020' for local roads. Compare raw, never parse.

37._comment: 1201628 segments, the richest state inventory found: StreetName on 1166779 (97%), SrfcType on 918124, ImprvDate on 473065 and OwnerName on 297234 naming 1049 bodies from Charlotte down. NCDOT is also the ONLY agency probed anywhere that publishes coded-value domains, so ImprvType, OwnerType, FuncClass and SrfcType are decoded from the agency's own words rather than inferred - see CodeTables.ncdotImprovement. Ownership needs two rules because the level and the body live in OwnerType and OwnerName while NCDOT's own maintenance is declared in a third field, RouteMaintCode = System, on 607062 segments naming no owner at all; reading a blank as 'state' would be a guess where the agency published an answer. ImprvDate is clean - 1872 distinct dates, the largest 4.0% - so unlike San Antonio, Laredo and Arlington it needs no sentinel filter.
37.dateCaveat: NCDOT records the last improvement on about 470,000 of its 1.2 million road segments, and what kind of work it was.

39._comment: 402947 segments with a jurisdiction on every one and a real street name on 379684 (94%). This is NOT the Ohio layer rejected in section 10.3: that one was 58127 rows whose LAST_CONST was the 1900-01-01 placeholder, on a server that now 404s. This one publishes no construction date at all - PERP_YEAR is the dataset's own vintage, 2022 on 100% of rows, and RESURFACE_ covers 9228 segments across only 2020-2022 - so nothing dated is mapped rather than dressing up a publication year as a build year. The name is stored in three fields and needs joining. SURFACE_TY is single undocumented letters (G on 64%) and is deliberately not read.
39.dateCaveat: Ohio publishes who is responsible for each road but no construction or resurfacing history.

25._comment: 409586 statewide segments, and the SECOND agency in this survey to publish coded-value domains - thirty of them, including JURISDICTN and SURFACE_TP. Its jurisdiction list is the most complete found anywhere: it separates the Department of Conservation and Recreation, Massport, four branches of the military, the Army Corps and the BIA. Two values carry real weight: H marks a road private, and 0 marks one 'unaccepted by city or town' on 120329 segments - a fifth of the state - which is the same distinction Maricopa draws with countyCourtesy and maps to notPubliclyMaintained. F_CLASS here is the FHWA scheme but skips 4, so the shipped table covers it. No construction or resurfacing date is published. Note the field is STREET_NAME here; Boston's clipped copy of the same schema truncates it to STREET_NAM, and naming a field the layer does not have makes the service reject the whole query with a 400 rather than ignoring it.
25.dateCaveat: Massachusetts publishes who is responsible for each road, down to which are private or unaccepted, but no construction dates.

51._comment: 196896 routes. Virginia is arranged unlike any other state: VDOT maintains the secondary system in every locality except Arlington and Henrico, so RTE_JURIS_PROPER_NM names the LOCALITY a route sits in, not its owner, and reading it as ownership would hand 64076 VDOT-maintained secondary roads to the counties they run through. RTE_TYPE_NM is the ownership signal, and the arrangement proves itself: Arlington has 676 Street Routes to 7 Secondary, Henrico 6420 to 4, while VDOT-maintained Fairfax has 9422 Secondary to 5841 Street. So rule one claims every VDOT route type and declines Street Route; rule two then names the locality for what is left, and owner(named:) reads 'Fairfax County' as a county and 'City of Virginia Beach' as a municipality. No dates are published. RTE_COMMON_NM is a label rather than a name - 'Patrick Henry DR (NP - Arlington County)' on a street, 'SC-682E (Accomack County)' on a secondary route - so it is not read at all. The street parts are joined for named streets, and a secondary route with no street name falls through to TIGER, which gives a real one.
51.dateCaveat: Virginia publishes who is responsible for each route but no construction or resurfacing dates.

26._comment: 709036 segments, the largest state network shipped. Ownership is plain HPMS - 1 state (62038), 2 county (282098), 4 municipal (236976), plus 40 and 80 - so it needs no new table; 127663 rows carry none and claim no owner. NFC is the FHWA scheme and its 0 (116126 rows) is outside the published 1-7, so those yield no class rather than a wrong one. The name is in four fields and needs joining. No construction or resurfacing date is published: AADTYear dates the traffic count, not the road. Verified by spatial query at Detroit before shipping, because the search that found it also returned a layer named HPMS_state_roads_NV whose extent is Nevada.
26.dateCaveat: Michigan publishes who owns each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

36._comment: 394175 segments on layer 11, 'Maintenance Jurisdiction' - not the Federal Aid layers 1-4, which cover 16677 to 54221 each. SEGMENT_NAME is on 355159 (90%). NYSDOT is the THIRD agency found publishing coded-value domains, after NCDOT and MassDOT: fourteen of them here. OWNING_JURIS is the HPMS code space with New York's own labels (01 NYSDOT, 03 Town, 31 NYS Thruway, 26 Private) so the shipped hpmsOwnership table reads it, and 98/99 'to be investigated' fall outside it and claim nothing. OWNED_BY_MUNI_NAME names the body and is safe to attach: it is null on ALL 76742 NYSDOT rows and present on ALL 109379 city rows, so a state road can never be renamed after a municipality. FUNC_CLASS is deliberately NOT mapped - New York uses the two-digit extended scheme this repo has warned about since section 10, values running to 19, and the FHWA 1-7 table would decode them wrongly. No construction dates are published.
36.dateCaveat: New York publishes who maintains each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

21._comment: 480065 segments, every one named. Ownership_Status is NOT ownership - it is acceptance, and reads ACCEPTED on 479967 of 480065, which tells a reader nothing. Route_Type is the ownership signal: KY 382962, US 65034, I 15660 and PKWY 5640 are all Kentucky Transportation Cabinet, CITY 7869 is municipal, CNTY 2463 county, PRIV 21 private, FED 13 federal. Two rules because a city road needs its body named from City_Name ('Lexington') while a state route must not be renamed after the city it passes through. CNTY declines: County_Name is 'Hopkins' without the word County, so owner(named:) would read it as a municipality, and 2463 rows of 480065 is not worth a table to get right. PEND and OTHR decline too. No construction dates are published. Both rules list every route type, because a rule's names map is a rewrite table and not a whitelist: a value it does not mention falls through and is classified raw, which turned CNTY into a municipality called 'Cnty'.
21.dateCaveat: Kentucky publishes who is responsible for each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

19._comment: 359066 segments. OWNER_CODE is the plain HPMS space - 4 municipal (152954), 2 county (138861), 1 state (59765), plus 11, 12, 21, 62, 63 and 70 - so the shipped table reads it and 2372 rows carrying none claim nothing. Deliberately does NOT map a name: COMMON_NAME_1 prefixes the owner onto the road ('CITY OF DANA, ECKSTEIN STREET') and SHORT_COMMON_NAME_1 still trails a direction ('S AVENUE, N'), so TIGER's name is the better one and Iowa contributes ownership. SURFACE_TYPE is undocumented numeric codes (65, 20, 31) and is not read. No construction dates are published.
19.dateCaveat: Iowa publishes who owns each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

35._comment: New Mexico's HPMS submission as an event table: 2898383 rows, which is not 2.9 million roads but the same roads split at every attribute change. Verified as New Mexico rather than national - 9274 features around Albuquerque and zero at Austin, Chicago and San Francisco. Ownership is the plain HPMS space: 1 state (1527767), 4 municipal (361599), 2 county (145528), 26 private (33223), 50 tribal (9469), plus 11, 62, 64 and 80; 804586 rows carry none and claim nothing. Carries no name field at all, so TIGER names the road. The segmentation is the cost: a 150 m envelope returns 1840 features and about 350 KB even with outFields narrowed to three, which is the largest per-lookup payload of any profile shipped and the reason nothing beyond ownership and traffic is requested.
35.dateCaveat: New Mexico publishes who owns each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

13._comment: 872056 segments. Georgia was REJECTED in section 22 on a layer literally named HPMS that returned zero features in Atlanta - a Chattanooga tri-state regional extract. This is the real statewide inventory, found by a search aimed at MAINE, and verified the other way round: 504 features at Atlanta, 522 at Savannah, zero at Augusta Maine and Albany New York. Ownership is the plain HPMS space and its own STATE_ROUTE flag confirms it exactly - of 114425 rows coded 1 state, 114424 carry STATE_ROUTE=1, and county (412725), municipal (264595) and other-local (45720) are STATE_ROUTE=0 on all but four rows between them. Code 0 on 34591 rows is not a sixth class but unset data: 24795 of them are STATE_ROUTE=1, so it is a state road whose owner field was never filled. It is outside the HPMS space and claims nothing. FunctionalClass is one of the few fields anywhere with a published domain. street_nm is populated on 161717 rows - 90% of the state routes but only 5% of county roads - so it names the road where GDOT has a name and falls through to TIGER where it does not. No construction dates.
13.dateCaveat: Georgia publishes who owns each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

surfaceNames.3: Soil or graded and drained earth

50._comment: 77263 centrelines on layer 92, not 0. Ownership is the plain HPMS space and its shape is unlike any other state shipped: 3 town (44068) is the largest class, which almost nowhere else uses, and 26 PRIVATE is second at 16408 - more than a fifth of every road in Vermont - against 10702 state and 5205 municipal. Code 2 county is used ZERO times: Vermont's counties are judicial districts and keep no roads. RTNAME is self-describing and confirms the whole partition exactly: ownership 1 is VT/US/I signed routes (100%), 3 and 4 are both TH- town-highway numbers (98% and 100%), and 26 has no route number at all on 16406 of 16408 rows. Vermont also publishes domains for SURFACETYPE and AOTCLASS, which almost no service does - SURFACETYPE is decoded from its published domain, and its code 9 Unknown (12394 rows) is nulled rather than shown. RTNAME's '-' placeholder on 16731 rows is nulled too so it can never be mistaken for a road's name. No construction dates.
50.dateCaveat: Vermont publishes who owns each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

30._comment: 238768 centrelines, the NG911 framework Montana assembles from its counties. Ownership carries a PUBLISHED domain - City, County, Federal, Private, Public, State, Tribal - which almost no service does, so the levels are read rather than derived. It is also null on 187758 rows (78.6%), so Montana names an owner for 51010 roads and stays silent on the rest rather than guessing; the null rows still get their name from the layer and their owner from no one. Public (3097) names no level and claims nothing. The name is split across four fields in Title Case (South + Montana + Avenue) and is joined, not picked from. SurfaceType is a published domain too - Dirt, Gravel, Paved - and its Unknown is nulled. No construction dates.
30.dateCaveat: Montana publishes who owns about a fifth of its roads and no construction dates.

46._comment: 150179 segments served from SDDOT's OWN server at sdgis.sd.gov, not ArcGIS Online - the first state found that way, and the reason the plan says to try the state DOT's server before concluding nothing exists. LOCAL_SYSTEM carries a published domain and is the richest local vocabulary shipped: 7 city street (54576), 6 TOWNSHIP system (38361), 4 county (25883), 3 county SECONDARY (14262), 8 ROAD DISTRICT (3051). South Dakota is the only state shipped that separates a county secondary road from a county road or names a road district. Its 99 Not Attributed (7827) is mostly the state trunk system, which DATA_CLASS=1 identifies properly - hence two rules, LOCAL_SYSTEM first and DATA_CLASS second, so state highways are answered by the field that knows. FUNC_CLASS is the two-digit extended scheme (01-19) like New York and must NOT use the FHWA table, so it is not mapped. FED_DOMAIN names who federally administers the land, not who keeps the road, so it is not mapped either. No construction dates.
46.dateCaveat: South Dakota publishes who keeps each road but no construction or resurfacing dates.

33._comment: 111680 segments on layer 5, not 0, served from NH GRANIT at nhgeodata.unh.edu. The same inventory also appears inside a VERMONT Amtrak study on ArcGIS Online; this is the first-party publication and is used instead. OWNERSHIP is a trap - it reads TOWN and PRIVATE on most rows but numeric patrol codes (611, 325, 324) on the state ones, so it is not mapped. LC_LEGEND is the clean field: exactly 7 values covering every row, no codes - Local 60621, Private 25985, State 21291, NOT MAINTAINED 3351, Federal 306, Recreation 111, Out of state 15. Its Not Maintained count matches LEGIS_CLASS VI exactly, which is New Hampshire's Class VI road: a public right of way the town has voted to stop maintaining, and the one honest answer is that nobody keeps it. Recreation and Out of state name no authority and claim nothing. FUNCT_SYSTEM is the plain FHWA 1-7. No construction dates.
33.dateCaveat: New Hampshire publishes who keeps each road, including its unmaintained Class VI roads, but no construction dates.

name: RDWAY_NAME
nullStrings: REFER CENTER LINE LAYER FOR ROAD NAME

10._comment: 112446 segments on layer 2 of DelDOT's OWN server at firstmap.delaware.gov. MAINT_RSP_CODE was written off in an earlier batch as undecodable - no published domain, no self-describing field. The decode was in a SIBLING LAYER all along: layer 7 MAINTENANCE RESPONSIBILITY carries VALUE_TEXT in plain English, shaped '<owner> Road Maintained by <maintainer>' across eight values. Layer 7 is segmented by milepost, so joining on RDWAY_ID alone conflates stretches of one road that are kept by different bodies - a first attempt did exactly that and looked cleaner than it was. Restricting the join to the 13852 of 13969 road ids (99%) that carry exactly ONE text settles it: 'State Road Maintained by State' gave code 1 on 6000 of 6000 segments, 'Suburban Road Maintained by State' on 1669 of 1673, 'Municipal Road Maintained by Municipal Forces' gave 2 on 2191 of 2191, and all three '... Maintained by Other Forces' texts gave 3 on 210 of 210. So 1 is state (95762 rows, 85.2% - Delaware's state department maintains almost every road in the state, which is unusual and true), 2 is municipal (16198, 14.4%), and 3 (486, 0.4%) means kept by someone who is neither. 3 names no authority, so it declines rather than guessing. 239 segments under code 1 are actually maintained by the Delaware River and Bay Authority; they are a quarter of one percent and the state still owns the road. YEAR_LAST_IMP_DATE is a real improvement year on 61909 rows (55.1%), 19 distinct values over 1983-2025 with no sentinel. ACCEPT_YEAR_CODE (32039 rows, 1900-2004) is when the state ACCEPTED the road into its system, not when it was built - no field means that, so it is deliberately not mapped rather than dressed up as a construction date.
10.dateCaveat: Delaware publishes when a road was last improved, not when it was first built.

04013._comment: Order is load-bearing and reproduces the shipped v1 pipeline. The state entry for 04 runs first, so ADOT claims the interstate before the county source infers a municipal owner for a pin inside Goodyear's limits. The centreline entry is what drive mode probes inside the county: it is the county's own naming and it classifies in words ('Arterial') rather than TIGER's MTFCC codes. Layers 1/2/3 are Highway, Arterial and Local; there is no combined layer and a group layer cannot be queried.

48061._comment: 3119 segments of unincorporated Cameron County road, the county's own inventory. Carries STREET, SURFACE, No_Lanes, SUBDIVISIO and RIGHT_OF_W and NO dates of any kind. Presence in this layer is itself the ownership answer - it is the county's maintained-road list, the same inference MCDOT's layer 2 supports - but it is left unmapped because the layer publishes no ownership field to read and inferring from silence is a judgement the catalog cannot express.
48061.dateCaveat: Cameron County publishes its road inventory without any construction or resurfacing dates.

4819000._comment: 38564 supersegments. rehab_year is populated on 27588 across 95 distinct years with NO dominant value — the largest is 2024 at 8.4% — so unlike San Antonio's InstallDate it needs no sentinel filtering. rehab_type is a 21-value vocabulary decoded by CodeTables.workKind(pavementTreatment:), shared with Denver; 'None' on 11007 rows means no recorded work and yields no entry. maint_resp is 'City' on 38471 of 38564, so namedAgency reads it as a municipality; it is the level, not the body, which is the same amount PennDOT's JURIS=5 claims. The City of Dallas spans five counties, which is why this is keyed on place GEOID and not county FIPS.
4819000.dateCaveat: Dallas records when a street was last rebuilt or resurfaced, not when it was first built.

4865000.displayName: City of San Antonio pavement inventory
4865000._comment: 98986 segments. InstallDate is populated on ALL of them and 96% of it is placeholder: 2000-01-01 on 49782 rows (50.3%) and 1980-01-01 on 45272 (45.7%), leaving 3932 real dates. Both epoch values are in nullNumbers; without them the app would invent a construction year for every street in the city. What is genuinely populated is Owner, 43 values naming the body — San Antonio, Bexar County, TxDOT, Private on 11017 segments, Ft Sam Houston, Lackland AFB — decoded by CodeTables.owner(named:). Surface_Type is 'TBD' on 42576 rows, hence nullStrings.
4865000.dateCaveat: San Antonio dates only about 3,900 of its 99,000 street segments; the rest carry a placeholder the app discards rather than shows.

4857200._comment: 3611 segments. OWNER is populated on all of them and names CITY, COUNTY and so on, read by CodeTables.owner(named:). Repave_Date is a plain year on 501 segments and its values are exactly 2015-2018, so it is a repaving programme record rather than a construction history; MAINTENANCE_REPAIRS names the treatment and workKindDefault files it as upkeep, never as what built the street. PAVEMENT_RATING is a 1-10 score, not the 0-100 PCI the other cities publish.
4857200.dateCaveat: Pharr records its 2015-2018 repaving programme, not when its streets were first built.

4822660._comment: 418 project polygons, matched by containment rather than nearest line because a project area is half a mile across and the distance from a pin inside it to its boundary exceeds the on-road gate. Uniquely rich for a city: CONTRACTOR, CONSTRUCTION_ACTUAL and ACTUAL_COMPLETION on 139 completed projects, plus a written DESCRIPTION. Projects still in design carry a future ACTUAL_COMPLETION, which RoadWork.isPlanned separates.
4822660.dateCaveat: Edinburg publishes its capital projects, so a street shows only work the city has funded as a project.

4877272._comment: 4175 segments. Names the street and the jurisdiction responsible for it and publishes NO dates. Listed because naming the responsible body is a real answer where the alternative is TxDOT's blanket municipal code.
4877272.dateCaveat: Weslaco publishes its street centreline without construction or resurfacing dates.

4810768._comment: 8581 centrelines for the largest Rio Grande Valley city, carrying a name and a STREET_USE and no ownership or dates. The thinnest profile shipped, and it earns its place only because Brownsville's own naming beats TIGER's inside the city. NAME is the full form ('E ELIZABETH ST') and UNIQUE_NM is the bare stem ('ELIZABETH'), so the order matters. The layer answers spatial queries but returns nothing for an attribute-only one, which is harmless here because every query this app makes is an envelope.
4810768.dateCaveat: Brownsville publishes a street centreline only: no ownership and no dates.

4845384._comment: 346 annexation tracts covering the city, Year 1927-2023, Annex_Date on 337 and Ord_no on 340 (the oldest reads CHARTER). McAllen is the largest Rio Grande Valley city and publishes no street inventory, no pavement layer and no capital-project register; its Subdivision_Master carries a Developer name but holds only 40 polygons, too few to be worth a profile. Annexation is not a construction date and the app never shows it as one - it renders in the paper trail beside the plat - but it bounds when the streets in a tract could have gone in, and it is the only dated fact the city publishes. Annex_Date is negative epoch milliseconds before 1970, which the accessor handles.
4845384.dateCaveat: McAllen publishes no street or project records; what is shown is when the city annexed the land, which is not when the road was built.

4841464._comment: 10627 segments, and one of very few sources anywhere publishing an actual YEAR_BUILT rather than a resurfacing date. 1980 is a placeholder on 5405 of them - 50.9%, against a smooth 2%-per-year spread across the other 53 distinct values - so it is filtered, the same call made for San Antonio's InstallDate. That leaves about 5200 genuine construction years. OWNER is 'CITY OF LAREDO' on every row. BRANCHNM is the assembled name ('ALBANY DR'); FENAME and FETYPE hold the parts separately and would need joining.
4841464.dateCaveat: Laredo publishes a construction year for about half its streets; the other half carry a 1980 placeholder the app discards rather than shows.

4804000._comment: 17359 segments carrying BOTH an install and a reconstruction date, which almost nothing else does. The fields named Built and Reconstructed are entirely null on every row and are NOT the ones to read; Installed (13125 populated) and Replaced (13321) are. Each carries one bulk-loaded default: 1908-06-09 on 2209 Installed rows and 2008-06-12 on 1370 Replaced rows, single exact dates against roughly 1280 distinct values spread under 1% each, so both epochs are filtered. Custodian names the responsible body and covers slivers of Pantego, Kennedale, Dalworthington Gardens, Mansfield and Grand Prairie as well as Arlington's own 12984.
4804000.dateCaveat: Arlington records when a street was installed and when it was last replaced; about a quarter of its segments carry neither.

4837000._comment: 9133 centrelines. Publishes no construction date of any kind - MODIFIEDDATE is a GIS edit stamp - and earns its place purely on ownership: OWNERSHIP names CITY 5934, STATE 2182, PRIVATE 820, plus slivers owned by DFW airport, Dallas and Coppell. TxDOT files every one of these as a bare municipal code, so naming the body is the whole contribution, and 820 private streets is a real answer TxDOT cannot give. MAINTBY is a 1/-1/-2 code with no published meaning and is not read.
4837000.dateCaveat: Irving publishes who owns each street but no construction or resurfacing dates.

0820000._comment: 29728 segments on layer 428, not 0. Jurisdiction and Maintenance both name the body, and Maintenance is the finer of the two - it separates DIA, Denver Parks and Recreation and Fairmount Cemetery from the city proper, and marks 1054 segments PRIVATE where Jurisdiction marks 2112. Read in that order for that reason. YR_LSTWK is the year the city last worked the segment: 24458 of 29728 (82%) across a smooth spread from the 1990s with no dominant value, so no sentinel filter is needed. It is maintenance, never construction - CCD_Treatment names the treatment - so workKindDefault is maintained. FROMNAME and TONAME are not mapped as cross streets: they run to whole sentences listing ramps and signals.
0820000.dateCaveat: Denver records when it last worked on a street, not when the street was built.

2148000._comment: 24327 segments. Found while searching for INDIANA: the scan returned it because the org is unlabelled, and its owner names - JEFFERSONTOWN, SHIVELY, MIDDLETOWN, 'OUT OF JEFFERSON' - are Jefferson County KENTUCKY suburbs. It returns zero features at Indianapolis and 171 at downtown Louisville. The third cross-state false positive of the batch, and the reason every candidate is now checked at an in-state pin. OWNER_NAME is METRO on 24174 rows plus 111 PRIVATE and a handful of independent suburbs; 'OUT OF JEFFERSON' declines rather than naming a body it does not know. FiscalYear is null on 23173 of 24327, so almost nothing carries a date and ProfileMapping drops an undated work entry.
2148000.dateCaveat: Louisville records pavement condition for every street but a paving year for only about a thousand of them.

4159000._comment: 92464 centrelines published by TriMet for the Portland metro. ROADOWNER names 33 bodies outright - City of Portland 37314, Washington County 8314, City of Hillsboro 5179, Oregon Department of Transportation 2774 - and owner(named:) reads every shape it uses without a rename table: a trailing 'County' gives a county, 'Department of Transportation' the state, and a city name a municipality. 'Unknown' on 3224 rows is a null string and claims nothing. Keyed to Portland's place GEOID even though the layer covers the whole metro, which under-uses it at the edges but can never answer for a city it does not cover. Oregon publishes no statewide roadway service, so this is the state's only entry. No dates.
4159000.dateCaveat: Portland publishes who owns each street but no construction or resurfacing dates.
